title: ConduitStream handbook: ergonomic Dual-Consumer adapter for AsyncIterator <-> ReadableStream + retry/checkpoint semantics
creator: Asha Menon
description: Ship a developer-friendly adapter (ConduitStream) that exposes a single server-driven stream as both a TypeScript AsyncIterator and a Web ReadableStream with consistent cancellation, backpressure, and retry/resume semantics.
background: Teams building low-latency UIs and server-side pipelines struggle with shape differences between AsyncIterator and Web ReadableStream. Existing examples are fragmented (one-offs for consumers) and lead to duplicate network connections, inconsistent cancellation, and surprising retries. This ticket consolidates previous experiments into a defined adapter + playbook for the TS SDK.
goals: 1) Provide a single ergonomic primitive that can be consumed as an AsyncIterator or a ReadableStream without duplicating the underlying connection. 2) Ensure cancellation semantics propagate to the server promptly. 3) Define safe retry/resume primitives using checkpoint tokens and idempotent chunk windows. 4) Publish usage examples, tests, and a migration plan.
non_goals: Do not attempt to spec server-side resume protocols here beyond a minimal checkpoint token (server already emits resumeToken). Not adding new wire-level protocol changes that require infra deploys.
proposed_api:
- class ConduitStream<T> implements AsyncIterable<T> { [Symbol.asyncIterator](): AsyncIterator<T>; toWebStream(): ReadableStream<T>; cancel(reason?: string): void; getResumeToken(): string | null; }
- client.streamConduit(request): ConduitStream<Chunk>
- client.retryFrom(token): ConduitStream<Chunk> // convenience wrapper around starting a new stream with resume token

Rationale: keep the runtime surface minimal. ConduitStream owns a single transport session; both consumer forms share the same async source and buffers. cancel() triggers an abort to the transport and drains pending consumers.

implementation_notes:
- Under the hood: single framed transport consumer that emits normalized Chunk objects. A small internal buffer (ring buffer) holds items for short-lived concurrency. toWebStream() converts from async source using standard ReadableStream constructor and wires backpressure to the internal buffer size.
- Cancellation: ConduitStream.cancel() aborts the transport and rejects pending iterator 'next' calls with a designated CancelledError. Web stream readers get closed.
- Retries: server emits resumeToken at safe checkpoints (token marks the last completed top-level token boundary). SDK documents an 'at-most-once chunk replay' guarantee: resumed streams may re-emit chunks ended at the checkpoint. Users should dedupe by token or id if they need strict idempotence.
- Browser/Node differences: use native ReadableStream on platforms where available; fallback to web-stream-polyfill in older Node runtimes. Test matrix below.
tradeoffs:
- Single-connection model simplifies resource usage but makes concurrent independent consumers (two different parts of app reading at different rates) share the same cursor; we prefer this because duplicate connections were the bigger pain.
- Resume semantics rely on server-provided tokens. If server teams change token granularity, SDK will provide knob to configure 'resumeGranularity' at client creation.
- Implementing full exactly-once replay is expensive; we document dedupe patterns instead.
test_plan:
- Unit: ConduitStream next()/toWebStream() interop tests, cancellation propagation, abort reason mapping.
- Integration: run against staging server that emits resumeToken; assert resumeFrom(token) continues from expected chunk.
- E2E: browser sample app that toggles between iterator and stream consumption. Measure no extra network streams created.
- Load: concurrency test with 1000 short-lived consumers to validate internal buffer eviction and socket reuse.
- Compatibility: Node 18/20, Deno 1.37, Chrome stable.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge API behind feature flag in TS SDK (alpha). 2) Publish 0.1.0-beta package and sample app. 3) Add a migration guide for existing streaming helpers. 4) Coordinate with SDK docs + Console examples. 5) Monitor errors/metrics for 2 weeks then GA.
dependencies: infra:server-emit-resumeToken (no infra change required; server already emits tokens but we rely on stable format)
